messages:
sasha: Heads-up — seeing a latency regression on Dedicated GPUs for seqlen ~512-1024 when KV cache is enabled. Traces show kernel selector picking smem_tile_v2 which has very high reg usage and lower throughput in that range.
kevin: Can you paste the perf counters / a short nvprof flame?
sasha: Quick profile snippet:```
model: redwood-llama-13b
device: a100-80gb
kernel: smem_tile_v2
occupancy: 0.45
regs_per_thread: 64
dyn_smem_bytes: 49152
active_warps: 10
achieved_tflops: 5.2
latency_p95: 18.9ms
```Fallback kernel smallbatch_fastpath shows latency_p95 ~13ms for same shape.
maya: Is this on A100 or H100? driver/runtime?
sasha: A100, CUDA 11.8, driver 535. Reg pressure seems to come from a fused attention+softmax vectorize change we rolled last week. Kernel picker rule currently asserts: if seqlen > 256 and batch>1 -> prefer smem_tile. That heuristic doesn't account for increased regs from fusion + KV cache.
tony: Could be the KV cache increases per-thread state (keeps extra pointers) so effective regs blow up. Idea: add an occupancy-aware penalty term to the selector that uses estimated regs_per_thread and dynamic_smem to compute a score. Also sample seqlen histogram from live traffic to avoid hard thresholds.
kevin: I tried a small tweak locally: lower smem preference weight and add reg_penalty. Simple microbench: before patch p95=18.2ms, after p95=12.9ms for seqlen 768 batch=2. Throughput unchanged.
sasha: Nice — can you paste the quick patch/config you used?
kevin: config I used (local test harness):```json
{"kernel_selector": {"smem_weight": 0.8, "reg_penalty": 1.25, "seqlen_sample_count": 100, "occupancy_floor": 0.35}}
```Applied as override in runtime.canary.
maya: We should also revisit batching heuristics. Current packer bins by total_tokens, which mixes active tokens and KV tokens. For KV-heavy traffic that inflates token counts but not compute (since KV is reused), packer ends up picking tiles that expect more smem. I propose splitting into active_tokens vs kv_tokens and prioritize active_tokens for tiling decisions.
tony: Agreed. Also add a quick estimator: estimated_dynamic_smem = base_smem + kv_tokens * kv_smem_per_token + seqlen_window * misc. Use that in selector scoring.
sasha: Can someone run a 24h canary on dedicated-spot pool with the selector change + packer tweak? We'll collect p50/p95 and counter for regs_spill and smem_coworkers.
perf-bot: Auto-profile job #3172 finished: baseline p95=17.9ms, patch p95=12.8ms, mean CPU util down 3%. No new regression alerts.
kevin: Results from my local canary (30m): p50 improved ~20%, p95 improved ~28%, reg_spill counter dropped to near-zero in these shapes.
maya: Great. For rollout: 1) formalize occupancy-aware scoring (TONY), 2) split token accounting in packer (MAYA), 3) canary on dedicated pool for 48h (SASHA+KEVIN), 4) emit perf counters to Console and add an eval prompt to catch regression in next deploy.
tony: I'll draft the scoring formula and add unit tests that simulate increased regs_per_thread and dyn_smem scenarios. Quick sketch: score = latency_est / (throughput_est * (1 + reg_penalty*(regs/ideal_regs) + smem_penalty*(dyn_smem/ideal_smem))). Will iterate.
sasha: I'll open the PR with the test harness and a microbench job that runs on a100/h100 profiles. Tagging @kevin for the canary conf and @maya for packer change.
kevin: Will push the canary override and monitor. Thanks! :rocket:
maya: I'll prototype the packer split today — will post results.
perf-bot: Canary monitor: canary-2179 ran 6h so far. p95 delta -29%. No spike in errors.
kevin: re: telemetry — we should log selector decisions per-request (small sample) so we can correlate selector choice -> perf counters later. Add a sample_rate config.
sasha: Agreed. Add sample_rate=0.005 for production.
kevin: thanks all.
sasha: Closing loop: if canary stable by EOD tomorrow we roll to 10% then 50%.
